situation.note: my mother in law keeps saying once the baby comes you will anyway leave all this CA work. I built my practice from zero. my husband just changes the subject. I feel like I am slowly being erased

understanding.bridge: The life you built from zero is what the Gita calls your own dharma: a duty that no one else can do, and no one else can take from you.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being told you will disappear to standing in the truth of what you are and what you built.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being erased, and the anger of it, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: A CA who built her practice from zero is being told by her mother-in-law that she will leave it after the baby, while her husband stays silent and she feels herself being erased.
understanding.mirror: You feel like you are slowly being erased while your husband changes the subject.
understanding.insight: You are being handed a smaller picture of yourself than the one you live, and the smallness is theirs.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

I feel anxious most of the time

queries.hook: Being told the life you built will end, and the anger of watching yourself be erased while the one beside you says nothing. Tension with my in-laws.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture shows their smallness; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; they do not decide your worth, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A woman of learning and standing, dismissed by her husband's family, who questioned them openly and stood in her truth until they had no answer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, telling him to lift himself up by his own mind. A person can be their own best friend, or their own worst enemy. The choice is entirely their own. This means you do not have to wait for others to see your worth. You can choose to stand by yourself, steady and clear, even when the world around you turns away.
verse.for_you: The life you built from zero is your own dharma, a duty no one else can do. Your in-laws are handing you a smaller picture of yourself, but the smallness is theirs. Your partner stays silent, and they try to erase you. Stand on your own side.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you feel yourself shrinking and stand up straight.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your office, and you are told you will soon be gone.
asks: What does it mean to be my own best friend right now?
How do I lift myself up when others push me down?
Can I be my own enemy if I let their words win?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the section on wealth: how the world treats someone who has lost money.
verse.sanskrit: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
verse.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
verse.translation: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
verse.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.
verse.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from a section on wealth. He says that a person's faculties, mind, and voice do not change when they lose money. Yet the world treats them as a different person. The verse points out that money alters others' perception, not the person's true nature. The value of what they built remains, even if others refuse to see it.
verse.for_you: Your in-laws see your practice as a temporary phase because they wish it to be. The life you built from zero is your own dharma, and no one else can do it. Their silence does not erase your work.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when your work proves your worth, not their opinion.
verse.scene_line: You are the same mind and voice, yet they treat you as someone else.
asks: How do I see myself when they refuse to see me?
Can I separate their view from my own reality?
What part of me remains unchanged by their dismissal?

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.setting: Yama on the inner self and the world's pain.
verse.sanskrit: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुः न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥
verse.line: The sun shows every flaw yet stays untouched. Your deepest self stays untouched by the world's sorrow.
verse.translation: Just as the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the flaws the eyes see outside, so the one inner self of all beings is not stained by the sorrow of the world; it stands apart.
verse.why: Look inward; what lasts is not out there among passing things.

prasang.title: Turning the gaze inward
prasang.summary: In the second half of his teaching, Yama explains that our senses face outward, so we miss what is within. The wise turn inward and stop looking for lasting things among passing ones; when the knots of the heart are cut, a person is free.
prasang.lesson: Look inward; what lasts is not out there among passing things.

verse.meaning: Yama tells the boy Nachiketa that the sun sees every flaw yet remains untouched by them. He says the one inner self of all beings is not stained by the sorrow of the world, and it stands apart. The wise turn inward and stop looking for lasting things among passing ones. When the knots of the heart are cut, a person is free.
verse.for_you: You are being erased, but your inner self is not stained by what your in-laws say. Look inward. What you built from zero is lasting. The world's sorrow does not touch your core. You are your own witness.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you did today that no one else can do.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your own light while others look away.
asks: How do I stop their words from staining me?
How do I see my own worth when they do not?
How do I cut the knot in my heart?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verse.sanskrit: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
verse.line: Let the waves of the world rise or fall. You, the ocean, neither gain nor lose.
verse.translation: In you, the boundless ocean, let the waves of the world rise or fall by their own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
verse.why: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

prasang.title: You are not your mind
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra drives home that Janaka is not the body, the doer, or the mind's likes and dislikes, but the ocean in which the waves of life rise and fall. He urges faith, an end to grief, and rest from endless deliberation.
prasang.lesson: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, who has been taught that his true nature is not his body or mind. The teacher says, let the world change around you. You are the deep ocean, and the world is only the surface waves. They rise and they fall. You do not grow or shrink with them. Your awareness stays the same. You do not have to become smaller to fit the room.
verse.for_you: The in-laws have drawn a smaller picture of you on their wall, but you built the practice from zero. You are the ocean, not the wave. Let their words rise and fall without losing your depth. You do not need to shrink to fit their frame.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the ocean while they draw waves on the shore.
asks: How do I hold my depth when they try to shrink me?
Can I let their words pass without shrinking?

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

matched.label: I have to give someone bad news

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu is showing Nidagha what it means to be free while still living in the world. The free person does the work in front of them, whether it is pleasant or not, and treats everyone with the same steady mind. They speak gently and read what others truly mean, so they are not pulled under by the world's demands or its judgments.
verse.for_you: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
verse.try_today: Name one thing you built today that no one else can do.
verse.scene_line: You are reading their hearts while the subject changes.
asks: How do I read their hearts without losing myself?
What is the work in front of me today?

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated on the ground after losing his kingdom. He believes his life is over and wants to give up. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt, not to settle for little, and to stop fearing. She says he must set his mind on what is truly good and pull himself together. She makes him see that the past failure does not define him. The results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed. She urges him to rise again and fight for what is his.
verse.for_you: Stand in your own truth and do your own duty from it; let their picture stay theirs, and let your conduct speak.
verse.try_today: Write down one professional goal that has nothing to do with their approval.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own kingdom, and someone is telling you to lie down and give it up.
asks: How do I stop shrinking when they look away?
What does it mean to fight for my own name?
How do I set my mind on what is truly good?

story.title: Satyakama Jabala, the honest boy
story.story_hook: Satyakama wanted to study, but first he had to ask his mother a question she could not answer.
story.summary: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.
story.lesson: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.

anchor.speaker: Jabala
anchor.setting: A boy asks his mother his lineage before seeking a teacher.
anchor.sanskrit: सा हैनमुवाच नाहमेतद्वेद तात यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि बह्वहं चरन्ती परिचारिणी यौवने त्वामलभे साहमेतन्न वेद यद्गोत्रस्त्वमसि जबाला तु नामाहमस्मि सत्यकामो नाम त्वमसि स सत्यकाम एव जाबालो ब्रवीथा इति ॥
anchor.line: His mother said, 'I don't know your father's line. I am Jabala, you are Satyakama. Say exactly that.'
anchor.translation: She said to him: 'I do not know your lineage, my child. In my youth I moved about a great deal as a serving woman, and then I had you. So I do not know your lineage. My name is Jabala and your name is Satyakama. Just say you are Satyakama Jabala.'
anchor.why: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.

prasang.title: Satyakama Jabala, the honest boy
prasang.summary: A boy who wants to study asks his mother about his father's lineage. She tells him frankly she does not know, and he repeats this word for word to the teacher. The teacher accepts him for his honesty, sends him off with 400 weak cows, and the boy returns years later with a thousand, having learned from nature along the way, yet still asks his teacher to teach him.
prasang.story_hook: Satyakama wanted to study, but first he had to ask his mother a question she could not answer.
prasang.lesson: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.

story.hook_title: A boy didn't know who his father was, and told his teacher the truth anyway
story.teaser: A boy didn't know who his father was, and told his teacher the truth anyway
story.for_you: A CA who built a practice from zero is being told they will leave it after the baby. The husband changes the subject. The in-laws are writing a smaller picture of them than the one they live. The tradition says: you are not at fault. Stand firm. Act from dharma.
asks: What if I just stopped explaining my work to them?
How do I stand firm without breaking the home?
